title: Graceful client abort, server lease preemption, and tool-call fencing for OpenAI compatibility
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Production clients frequently issue mid-stream cancels (user hits stop or navigates away) while background tooling calls or function/tool invocations can still be in-flight. We saw two classes of failures in customer signals: (1) immediate server-side session eviction that caused tool calls to be delivered out-of-order or duplicated when clients rejoined, and (2) long-running server leases preventing capacity reclaim leading to degraded throughput on tail-heavy workloads. This PR introduces three coordinated behaviors to address those problems under the OpenAI-compat streaming surface: 1) soft-abort/hedge window — when a client cancels we mark the session as soft-aborted for a short hedging window (default 4s) during which the server will continue to finish in-flight tool calls but will stop emitting new tokens downstream. If the client re-establishes the same session ID within the window, we resume token emission in-order. 2) lease-based idle preemption — we add server-side session leases (ttl + last-active) and a conservative preemption policy that allows quick reclaim for idle noisy sessions while guaranteeing a quarantine period for recently-invoked tool calls. Leases expose an HTTP/OpenAI-compat header X-Redwood-Session-Lease allowing proxies and operators to surface lease state. 3) function-call fencing and idempotency gating — tool/function calls are fenced with a monotonic fence token per session and optional idempotency key; the server will not replay a tool invocation unless the fence advances or the client supplies the same idempotency key. This avoids duplicate tool runs across rejoin/resume scenarios. Implementation notes: - OpenAI-compat surface adds two optional headers and a session-level metadata bundle stored in the session manager; no changes to existing request/response shapes required. - Streaming handler now multiplexes a token-emitter and a tool-run tracker; the token-emitter respects the soft-abort state and will buffer but not emit tokens while a soft-abort is active. - SessionManager now persists minimal lease metadata in the runtime cache with a configurable preemption policy and quarantine window. - New config knobs: soft_abort_window_ms (default 4000), session_lease_ttl_ms (default 600000), tool_quarantine_ms (default 2000). Backwards compatibility: default values preserve current behavior for users who do not opt into session IDs; OpenAI-compat endpoints keep the same wire format and semantics unless a client includes the Redwood session headers. Tests and telemetry: unit tests for fence advancement, integration tests for reconnect/resume path with simulated tool-call latencies, and e2e load tests showing ~12% reduction in stale-session GPU occupancy under heavy reconnect churn. Rollout plan: staged feature flag behind openai_compat.session_lease; beginning with internal beta, then 10% host rollout, monitoring for functional regressions and tool-call duplication metrics.

release_notes: Adds soft-abort hedging window and session lease preemption to reduce stale sessions and avoid duplicate tool calls on reconnect. Introduces session fencing and idempotency gating for tool/function invocation and two optional OpenAI-compat headers (X-Redwood-Session-Id, X-Redwood-Session-Lease). Feature is behind a feature flag openai_compat.session_lease.
notes: Operator-facing docs updated; SDKs include helper to surface session header. Recommend running loadtest script before enabling wide rollout.
